desc.concept: boundary tokens before and inside code, markup, and citation fragments
desc.note: Windows span unrelated domains (C#, wiki categories, XML, Objective-C, prose, PHP) with no single shared token or pattern; the activation sits at varied structural positions.

desc.concept: bracketed mid-word fragments split across tokens
desc.note: Windows show varied mid-word splits (et, err, Cast, cam, exam, Park, sed, nerv, mut) in different domains, so the shared cue is a split word fragment rather than one topic.

desc.concept: digits and numeric values right after a bracketed token
desc.note: The marked token varies across unrelated text: numbers, word fragments, and punctuation, so no single symbol or word stands out.

desc.concept: subject pronoun after a clause break
desc.note: The marked token is the pronoun or infinitive marker right after a boundary, which varies across windows, so the pattern is weak and broad.

desc.concept: the token 'the' after 'In' in formal prose
desc.note: Mostly fires on 'In [the]' in formal prose, but also on other tokens like 'its', 'you', 'shootings', 'an', and 'shown'.

desc.concept: bracketed single-token insertion point in code and prose
desc.note: Windows share only a highlighted position inside varied code, prose, and markup; no consistent topic, token, or format.

desc.concept: text fragment right before a bracketed token
desc.note: Windows share no stable feature; the marked tokens vary widely across unrelated subjects and styles.

desc.concept: Bracketed sub-word fragment inside scientific and technical text
desc.note: Windows are heterogeneous (physics, sports, code, astronomy); the marked position is a varied word fragment rather than one stable token, so the pattern is weak.

desc.concept: scattered short tokens with no shared feature
desc.note: Windows span unrelated domains (medical training, C code, XML, Go, forum text) with no consistent token or theme.

desc.concept: bracketed token inside varied technical and medical text
desc.note: The marked tokens are heterogeneous (suffixes, function words, punctuation, digits), so the shared pattern is only the bracketed position itself.

desc.concept: the bracketed noun following 'its' or 'their' in academic prose
desc.note: Windows are varied in topic; the shared feature is a possessive pronoun followed by a noun, not one subject.

desc.concept: bracketed [[...]] markers around words in web text
desc.note: The marker wraps varied words (View, to, Hide, share, Posted, test) across unrelated sources, so the shared feature is a formatting artifact rather than a subject.

desc.concept: bracketed token inside code, markup, or technical text
desc.note: Windows span many unrelated domains (anime, C#, Python, LaTeX, medicine, math); the marked token varies (aki, Link, .makeText, ul, x, keras, ares, to, ,, <, *r), so the shared pattern is only that a split point falls inside a word or identifier.

desc.concept: double-bracket token marking a text insertion point
desc.note: Windows span unrelated topics (security audits, code, UPS systems, news); the shared feature is the literal "[[" marker, which is a source-formatting artifact rather than meaningful content.

desc.concept: bracketed or marked insertion points in code and text
desc.note: Windows span unrelated domains (SQL injection regex, Go tests, .htaccess, Kotlin, LaTeX, forum posts); the only shared trait is a double-bracket or marked token placed before a word, so the feature is weak.

desc.concept: legal-opinion text fragments at a split token
desc.note: Windows span many unrelated legal texts; the marked token falls at varied positions (e.g. 'erred', 'part', 'law', 'the', 'entitled'), with no single stable word or symbol.

desc.concept: bracketed token at the edge of varied phrases
desc.note: The bracketed spans fall on unrelated words (layer, info, Center, intake, intervention, ist, Channel, Input, region), with no shared lexical item, topic, or format.

desc.concept: Bracketed token inside varied text, mostly after short prefixes
desc.note: The bracketed spot falls on different tokens across windows (VIS, em, 设计, Mem, arm, M, 8, Sim, memor, F, 0, 1, Mor), so no single symbol or word recurs; the shared trait is only the marked position.

desc.concept: bracketed highlighted token inside mixed text and code
desc.note: Windows span unrelated domains (code, error logs, news, science, SQL); the marked spot varies with no stable shared token or feature.

desc.concept: words right after a marked bracket token
desc.note: Windows are unrelated topics; the only shared feature is a bracket marker placed mid-text, with no consistent word or meaning.

desc.concept: single-token position inside varied text windows
desc.note: Windows span unrelated domains (medicine, code, finance, cooking, music, Kuwait study) with no shared word, syntax, or format; the marked token is a different ordinary word or symbol each time.

desc.concept: double slash or slash token in code and math
desc.note: The highlighted marks are varied: slashes, equals signs, commas, and words in prose, code, and math. No single stable feature is visible.

desc.concept: text-internal [[ ]] or [[ of]] insertion point before a continuing word
desc.note: Windows span unrelated domains (ophthalmology affiliations, PHP code, legal boilerplate, sports, Danish prose, SCSS, Salesforce code) with no shared token, topic, or format; the only commonality is a bracketed insertion point at a word boundary, which is too generic to name a feature.

desc.concept: text immediately before a bracketed marked token
desc.note: Windows span unrelated languages and formats (English prose, C macros, HTML, R, Danish, Python, code, and fiction), with the marked position falling on varied tokens like 'never', 'compared', 'ils', '({', 'uv', and 'for'; no single stable feature is visible.

desc.concept: word fragments split at a token boundary
desc.note: Windows are unrelated across domains (album titles, academic text, French news, Norwegian news); the only shared trait is a bracketed partial word, which is too varied to name a stable feature.

desc.concept: mid-word or mid-token split points in code and prose
desc.note: Windows are unrelated: C#, Java, SCSS, HTML, and news text; the marked spot falls at varied places (a type name, a closing word, a sentence-internal word), with no shared symbol or structure.

desc.concept: mid-sentence connectors and digits before a break
desc.note: Windows share no stable feature; the marked tokens vary widely (conjunctions, punctuation, digits, code, chemistry), so no single consistent pattern is supported.

desc.concept: bracketed token at varying positions in mixed text
desc.note: Windows span unrelated languages, domains, and code; the marked position is a different character each time with no consistent symbol or pattern.

desc.concept: mid-word or mid-token split inside code and text
desc.note: The windows share only a placeholder-like insertion point; the highlighted spans are unrelated tokens (digits, punctuation, names, code identifiers), so no single stable feature is supported.

desc.concept: mid-sentence 'there' and 'that/those' as pronoun or placeholder
desc.note: Windows share only the frequent word 'there' or demonstratives at varied positions across unrelated topics; no stable feature is clear.

desc.concept: arbitrary token inside math problems and code
desc.note: Windows span unrelated domains (math exercises, Kotlin, publishing, C#, news) with no shared token or topic; the highlighted spots fall on different symbols each time.

desc.concept: scattered subword and punctuation fragments in varied text
desc.note: Windows span Spanish, Danish, code, and citations with no shared word, symbol, or structure; the activation points at mixed positions rather than one feature.

desc.concept: Bracketed token inserted mid-word or mid-phrase
desc.note: Windows are unrelated: code, news, science abstracts, forum posts; the marked spot varies with no shared feature.

desc.concept: bracketed markers at boundaries in mixed text
desc.note: Windows span code, academic papers, news and forum text; the shared feature is a [[ ]] marker placed at varied token positions, not one subject.

desc.concept: token just before a line break or bracket
desc.note: Windows are unrelated code, French and English prose; the activating token is a varied boundary position, not one stable feature.

desc.concept: Bracketed token at a varied mid-text position
desc.note: The windows share no stable feature: the marked tokens span finance, legal text, code, medicine and prose, with no recurring symbol or word.

desc.concept: bracketed marked token in varied text
desc.note: Windows are heterogeneous; the marked token varies (/libs, /batim, @hotmail, Snapdragon, poke), with no single stable feature beyond the bracket marking.

desc.concept: text fragments ending right before a bracketed highlighted token
desc.note: The windows span many unrelated subjects and formats (Greek sports news, Go code, Turkish election results, science abstracts, product reviews), with no shared word, symbol, or structure that recurs across them.

desc.concept: mid-word or mid-phrase token break before a continuation
desc.note: Windows are heterogeneous: code template, medical, legal, and Spanish text; the marked positions share only that the next token is a continuation of a word or phrase.

desc.concept: the token "de" inside words, often split from a longer word
desc.note: Activation falls on a mid-word fragment "de" in varied contexts (Perry, deicing, deletion, depletion), with a few unrelated spots on other tokens.
